--- title: Life Expectancy author: MARL date: Jul-2026 format: html theme: sketchy categories: [Python, 26Winter, "data: gapminder.csv"] --- ## The data set I am using the gapminder data for this project. ## First look at the data Open the data as a dataframe and look at the shape ::: {#74958890 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd df = pd.read_csv("../../../../data/gapminder.csv") s = df.shape print(f'There are {s[0]} rows and {s[1]} columns') c_names = df.columns.tolist() print("The headings are: ") for c in c_names: print(f'- {c}') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` There are 1704 rows and 6 columns The headings are: - country - year - pop - continent - lifeExp - gdpPercap ``` ::: ::: Get a summary of the numerical data ::: {#472ba068 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.describe() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Check for null values and data types. ::: {#c24151f6 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} df.info() print("There are no null values that would have been removed in data cleaning.") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` RangeIndex: 1704 entries, 0 to 1703 Data columns (total 6 columns): # Column Non-Null Count Dtype --- ------ -------------- ----- 0 country 1704 non-null object 1 year 1704 non-null int64 2 pop 1704 non-null float64 3 continent 1704 non-null object 4 lifeExp 1704 non-null float64 5 gdpPercap 1704 non-null float64 dtypes: float64(3), int64(1), object(2) memory usage: 80.0+ KB There are no null values that would have been removed in data cleaning. ``` ::: ::: ### Unique values for potential catagories Check Country first ::: {#e89395a6 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} all_countries = df.country.unique().tolist() print(f'This data has {len(all_countries)} different countries') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` This data has 142 different countries ``` ::: ::: Check Continent next ::: {#abfe2abb .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} all_continents = df.continent.unique().tolist() print(f"This data has {len(all_continents)} different continents") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` This data has 5 different continents ``` ::: ::: Also check years ::: {#fff18287 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} all_years = df.year.unique().tolist() print(f"This data has {len(all_years)} different years") for y in all_years: print(y) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` This data has 12 different years 1952 1957 1962 1967 1972 1977 1982 1987 1992 1997 2002 2007 ``` ::: ::: ### Summary We have data from 1952 to 2007 accross 142 countries and 5 continents. Each of these has population, life expectancy and GDP. I will see if I can find any links for life expectancy based on years. ## Years vs Life Expectancy ::: {#fb2ba8ba .cell execution_count=7} ``` {.python .cell-code} import seaborn as sns sns.catplot(data=df, x="year", y="lifeExp", kind="box") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](LifeExpReport_files/figure-html/cell-8-output-1.png){width=487 height=470} ::: ::: It appears that life expectancy increased with time but I will do a deeper dive ### Mean life expectancy by years ::: {#1352568c .cell execution_count=8} ``` {.python .cell-code} gb = df.groupby("year")["lifeExp"].mean() data = {"years" : all_years, "life" : gb } doggy = pd.DataFrame(data) sns.relplot(data = doggy, x = "years", y = "life", kind = "line") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![](LifeExpReport_files/figure-html/cell-9-output-1.png){width=470 height=470} ::: ::: ### Is the difference significant? Null hypothesis - there is no difference in life expectancy between 1957 and 2007 I will perform a ttest to check this ::: {#12bee4c3 .cell execution_count=9} ``` {.python .cell-code} import scipy.stats as stats early = df[df.year == 1957] late = df[df.year == 2007] check = stats.ttest_ind(early.lifeExp, late.lifeExp) print(f'The pvalue is {check.pvalue}.') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` The pvalue is 8.299952773896099e-23. ``` ::: ::: ### Result There is a very low pvalue indcating that we can reject the null hypothesis there is no difference in life expectancy between 1952 and 2007. ## Look at outlier 1992 ::: {#1be478e3 .cell execution_count=10} ``` {.python .cell-code} life_year = df[(df.year == 1992)] min_exp_92 = life_year.lifeExp.min() min_country = life_year.country[life_year.lifeExp == min_exp_92].tolist() print(f'The 1992 outlier is {str(min_country[0])} with a life expectancy of {min_exp_92}') ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` The 1992 outlier is Rwanda with a life expectancy of 23.599 ``` ::: ::: In 1992 there was a 100 day civil war in Rwanda that led to the genocide of nearly 1 million people.
